questions.question: Does the frozen formal sample contain a reviewer-blind opportunity to falsify both routing policies through shared no-manual misses?
questions.data_statement: Among the 120 formal cases, 34 cases have no-manual actions under both field_aware_simple_v1 and type_first_abstention_v1; they cover 15 severity and 19 affected-version cases.
questions.finding: The fixed formal set contains a shared-no-manual audit stratum without changing the formal allocation.
questions.bounded_implication: Future human conflict actions in these 34 cases can falsify a no-shared-miss assumption, but the stratum cannot identify a population shared-miss rate.
competing_explanations: Both policies may correctly avoid manual review on these cases.
Both policies may share a blind spot that only human actions reveal.
The cell-stratified sample may not represent the population rate.
questions.lineage_note: V3 concentrated its main comparison on policy-disagreement rows; V3.1 retained the formal set and explicitly sealed the existing 34-case shared-no-manual subset.
questions.stop_condition: Stop the label-free analysis after case counts, hashes, cell coverage, effective sample size, and the sample-conditional claim boundary are sealed.

questions.question: Does type_first_abstention_v1 preserve reviewer-specific manual-route coverage relative to the strong simple comparator while clearing the paired strategy-differentiation gate?
questions.data_statement: No human action labels exist; the label-free feasibility audit shows that a zero-loss one-sided 95 percent upper bound below 0.10 needs at least 29 conflict actions per reviewer.
questions.bounded_implication: Reviewer-consistent Branch P is not currently supported and will require both reviewers to pass the frozen paired-direction, event-floor, coverage, and manual-loss gates.
competing_explanations: Type-first may improve action alignment without losing manual-route coverage.
Any efficiency gain may be purchased through reviewer-confirmed missed escalations.
The number of human conflict actions may be too small to certify the selected margin.
questions.lineage_note: The manual-loss and coverage question was added before human exposure after the strong comparator and shared-blind-spot reviewer challenge; it is now a validity gate within routing-centric RQ3.
questions.stop_condition: Use only the two frozen reviewer passes; positive framing requires both reviewers to clear the 29-action, non-lower-coverage, and 0.10 exact-upper gates, otherwise route to boundary or ambiguity without adding cases.

questions.question: Can two different trained analysts apply the maintenance-action construct reliably enough to support the frozen RQ3 routing comparison?
questions.data_statement: V3.1 contains a presealed calibration-1 set, one conditional disjoint calibration-2 reserve, and 120 formal cases; no reviewer has received a packet.
questions.bounded_implication: The construct remains unqualified until two real independent reviewers complete the bounded calibration and formal stages.
competing_explanations: The guideline may support stable trained-analyst judgments.
Field context may be insufficient for a stable action construct.
Agreement may be driven by dominant labels rather than shared interpretation.
questions.lineage_note: V3.1 replaces the one-round V3 calibration with a single bounded revision-and-retry opportunity before formal exposure.
questions.stop_condition: Calibration-2 action raw agreement below 0.60 stops formal distribution; formal raw action agreement below 0.60 or nominal alpha below 0.40 forbids positive routing claims.
